label: Willow Creek Road Feeder 7 Lidar Extraction with Clearances
comments: Builds on lidar_terrain_layer_project.json (five connected poles, connected wires, field-measured sags, and a lidar-derived terrain layer applied to the 'Measured Design' design layer - see that example for the terrain layer rules) and adds clearance cases so SPIDAcalc checks NESC-style required clearances. Three case types are shown: 'Vertical to Ground' (wires over the ground environments along each span), 'Wire To Wire' (supply-to-communication separation midspan), and 'At Pole' (vertical separation between attachments on the pole). The same three cases appear twice on purpose: project-level defaultClearanceCases holds the project defaults used when new designs are created, and each design's clearanceCases holds the cases actually applied to that design - a design only runs the cases in its own list, so an imported file must repeat them per design (this mirrors what SPIDAcalc itself writes). Component groups in the cases match wires by usageGroups and industry ('Supply' = PRIMARY/SECONDARY/NEUTRAL utility wires, 'Communication' = communication wires), and the Vertical to Ground case's lower environments must equal environments defined in the client file and used on wireEndPoints[].environment: four spans here are 'STREET' and the WC-204 to WC-205 span is 'PEDESTRIAN' (a walking-path section), so the Street rows fire on the street spans and the Pedestrian rows fire on that last span. This environment mapping is where lidar land-use classification feeds the clearance analysis. Allowable values, wire states (thermal 'Energized 212F', physical 'NESC Medium Loaded'), and clearance distances are illustrative demo values, not engineering guidance. See doc/lidar_integration.md and the Clearance Cases section of doc/calc.md.

locations.label: WC-201
locations.comments: First pole of the run. Ground under the spans comes from the applied terrain layer, not terrainPoints.

locations.label: WC-202
locations.comments: Tangent pole. Through-running conductors are one wire per span, tied together with connectedWire.

locations.label: WC-203
locations.comments: Tangent pole at the bottom of the valley. The terrain layer's lowest points are along the adjacent spans.

locations.label: WC-204
locations.comments: Tangent pole climbing out of the valley. The span toward WC-205 follows a walking path, so both of its wire end points use the PEDESTRIAN environment and the Pedestrian rows of the Vertical to Ground clearance case apply to that span.

locations.label: WC-205
locations.comments: Last pole of the run. The incoming span from WC-204 is the PEDESTRIAN environment span.
